abstract: FluoMALDI imaging integrates fluorescence microscopy and matrix-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-MSI) of tissues and cells, leveraging matrix-enhanced fluorescence signals to enable spatially guided functional molecular discovery. Here we report three broadly applicable FluoMALDI paradigms that link how genes, proteins, and organelles shape spatial molecular composition. These advances are achieved by integrating immuno-, HaloTag-, and dye-based labels into a unified FluoMALDI imaging framework. These approaches enabled us to interrogate cell-specific lipidomic compositions in human hippocampal vasculature, neural crest cells in chick embryo tissue, and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived astrocytes. We also determined that fluorophore-MALDI matrix co-crystals resulted in FluoMALDI-induced fluorescence enhancements. Single-crystal X-ray crystallography showed that their co-crystallization produced localized, finite {pi}-{pi} interactions between two fluorophore molecules, or a fluorophore and a matrix molecule, throughout the crystal lattice. Together, these findings provide structural insight into the basis of fluorescence enhancement and support FluoMALDI as a broadly applicable multimodality imaging platform for biologically informed, cell-specific spatial-omics.
